title: NOC queue rows: new right-aligned util% column overlaps the Best-effort lane's queue-count digit
evidence: app/render/noc_overlay.odin:779 `bx := px + 52 + i32(lane) * 108`; :784 `draw_mono_c(v, fmt.tprintf("%d", q), bx + 22 + 70 + 4, ty, NOC_SIZE_BODY, NOC_TXT_DIM)`; :788 `util_r := px + NOC_PANEL_W - 6 - 96`; :798 `noc_col(v, fmt.tprintf("%d%%", p.util_pct), NOC_SIZE_BODY, util_col, util_r, ty)`. With NOC_PANEL_W :: 504 (line 333) and noc_col drawing left-anchored text ending at x_right (lines 510-512: `draw_mono_c(v, txt, x_right - w, y, size, col)`), the lane-2 digit box is [px+364, px+374.8] (IBM Plex Mono advance 600/1000 em, measured from assets/fonts/ibm_plex_mono_regular.ttf = 10.8 px/char at NOC_SIZE_BODY 18), while util_r = px+402 puts "100%" at [px+356, px+402] and "16%" at [px+368, px+402] — glyph overlap of ~5-16 px whenever util_pct >= 10.
detail: Every queue row draws all three lane counts (digit at px+364..375); the new util% right edge (px+402) makes 2+ digit values collide with that digit — worst at saturation ("100%"), the acceptance scenario. Not caught by tests or goldens: the rail is runtime-gated off the T2 capture path.
recommended_fix: Shift the util column right (e.g. util_r := px + NOC_PANEL_W - 6 - 48) or reserve the lane block's end (px+375) as the column's left bound, then re-verify with overlay-check.

title: New comments say the tray chip is 96 px, but this same diff widens TRAY_CHIP_W 96 -> 112
evidence: app/main.odin:2236 `// standard = 100 Mbps). Compact form fits the 96 px chip; the NOC rail` and core/units.odin:148 `// format_rate_compact — the tray-chip variant (the 96 px chip budget):` contradict app/render/tray.odin:13 `// constants so the port is faithful. 2026-08-23 (v2-network-units): 96 -> 112` and tray.odin:18 `TRAY_CHIP_W :: 112`.
detail: The change's own comments cite the pre-change chip width; a future reader sizing the compact label will use the wrong budget (96 vs the actual 112 px / 86 px text zone).
recommended_fix: Update both comments to reference the 112 px chip (86 px text zone) instead of 96 px.

title: "PIPES AT/OVER 90%" label and the pipe_red_pct=90 default restate the catalog tunable the predicate actually reads
evidence: noc_overlay.odin:820 `cur = noc_section(v, cur, scroll, visible, "PIPES AT/OVER 90% (HONEST)")` and :572 `noc_panel_rows :: proc(stats: ^pp.Stats_Record, events: []pp.Event, sel_pipe: i64, log_n: u32, pipe_red_pct: i32 = 90) -> i32 {`, while the filter is catalog-driven (:824 `if cat.balance.warnings.pipe_red_pct <= 0 || p.util_pct < u32(cat.balance.warnings.pipe_red_pct) {`) and data/balance.json:31 is `"pipe_red_pct": 90,`.
detail: ODN-5 (numbers single-source): the label and the default restate a tunable the code otherwise reads from balance.json; tuning pipe_red_pct makes the rail caption silently lie.
recommended_fix: Build the section title from the catalog value (fmt.tprintf("PIPES AT/OVER %d%% (HONEST)", cat.balance.warnings.pipe_red_pct)) and derive the measure default from the same source.

title: units.odin exports line_rate_bytes_per_tick with no production caller — only its own test references it
evidence: core/units.odin:81 `line_rate_bytes_per_tick :: proc(packet_bandwidth, capacity: u32) -> u32 {`; repo-wide grep finds the only references outside the definition in core/units_test.odin:30-32 (`testing.expect_value(t, line_rate_bytes_per_tick(120, 15), u32(187)) // 187.5 floors` etc.). stats.odin:207 computes util via `row.util_pct = util_pct_window(served_window, UTIL_WINDOW_TICKS, row.cap_units)` — capacity-units math, never this bytes-per-tick helper.
detail: The new canon module ships an exported helper nothing in app/ or core/ calls; despite its 'the honest utilization reference' comment, util_pct_window divides by cap×window, not by it.
recommended_fix: Either wire it into a display (e.g. the select readout's rate line) or fold it into the test module / drop it until it has a caller.
